title: the Babylonian mythos
audit_comment: THE BABYLONIAN MYTHOS - the D&DG walk round four, print pp. 22-25: ten beings (Anu, Anshar, Dahak, Druaga, Gilgamesh, Girru, Ishtar, Marduk, Nergal, Ramman) - the pantheon-wide cleric doctrine of the kilt and the tithe, and the ten stat blocks. Zero registry defs touched; the floor holds at 995. The flagged eyeball cells: the Dahak move (the 9 over 18 of the second-print extract against the 9 over 15 of the archive.org 1st print) and the Anu size (the 6 clean in both voices, the inch mark garbled).

banner.title: the Babylonian mythos - the D&DG walk round four, print pp. 22-25: ten beings from Anu the sky chief to Ramman the storm god - the cleric doctrine of the kilt and the tithe, the devil-world ruler Druaga, the three-headed dragon spirit Dahak, and the hero Gilgamesh.
banner.provenance: primary ink: the extract/ddg tesseract pass (commit cd645b4, pNNN_full.txt + pNNN_tsv.tsv, print = pdf - 1, pages 023-026; the second printing); the collation voice: the archive.org 1st-print derivative (djvu.txt + djvu.xml word geometry). The adjudications: the Gilgamesh two attacks (the IA xml word, clean, against the Termux 3 fold-garble), the Girru +3 axe (the IA voice against the Termux +43 garble), the Anu 2-20 (+7) damage line (the IA voice; the Termux fold ate the line), the Druaga charisma 4 (the single-glyph 15px TSV width against the 24px two-digit calibration), the Nergal 12 over 12 and the Ramman 12 over 48 moves (both voices), the Dahak length 72 feet (the IA foot mark against the Termux inch mark). The Dahak move pins the second-print extract 9 over 18 against the IA 1st-print 9 over 15 - flagged for the physical-copy eyeball.

bools.name: dgdOriginsExtremelyAncient
bools.comment: the origins of Babylonian mythology are extremely ancient

bools.name: dgdSourcesConflict
bools.comment: the consulted sources conflict with each other; the list is designed to be close to historically accurate and still playable

bools.name: dgdClericKilt
bools.comment: all Babylonian clerics wear the wraparound kilt of white with red cuneiform writing along the hem

bools.name: dgdClericsRearOfBattle
bools.comment: the clerics enter battle, but always in the rear of the action as support

bools.name: dgdAdvancementByPayment
bools.comment: advancement within a sect is through the payment of gold to the high priest court

bools.name: dgdPaymentNotLevel
bools.comment: the payment is not level advancement: ability increase does not guarantee temporal power

bools.name: dgdDangerousQuests
bools.comment: successful priests were given great and highly dangerous quests to prove their worthiness

bools.name: dgdNewMoonCeremony
bools.comment: the new moon is a time of great ceremony and a tithe paid to the temples to appease the gods

bools.name: dgdKingsQuestForRiches
bools.comment: kings are expected to go forth on quests with clerics and bring back riches to further the sect

bools.name: dgdMinorLawFasting
bools.comment: minor lawbreaking is punished by fasting, prayers, meditation and sacrifices until the deity signals forgiveness

bools.name: dgdMajorTransgressionSpells
bools.comment: major clerical transgressions are punished by complete denial of spells and excommunication

bools.name: dgdDemiHumansDemons
bools.comment: communicating with intelligent creatures or demi-humans is a crime - all are considered demons

bools.name: dgdQuestAtonement
bools.comment: an erring cleric may atone by taking up a quest aiding the sect in riches or power

bools.name: dgdHighPriestKing
bools.comment: the high priest is often the king and must be a magic-user/cleric of great power

bools.name: dgdAloofFromPopulace
bools.comment: clerical types remain aloof from the normal populace in temples and shrines

bools.name: dgdStatePoliticalWork
bools.comment: the clerics work to further the state politically as well as spiritually

bools.name: dgdAnuDistributesMoney
bools.comment: through Anu and the priest-king all shrine and temple money is dealt out, and political power through appointments

bools.name: dgdAnuSkyChief
bools.comment: Anu, god of the sky, chief of all the Babylonian deities, a greater god

bools.name: dgdAnuAppearsAsMan
bools.comment: this god appears as a man

bools.name: dgdAnuBreezeOfGaze
bools.comment: a strong breeze constantly blows in the direction of his gaze

bools.name: dgdAnuDisintegrationOnCast
bools.comment: beings casting things at Anu must save vs disintegration at -4 for both being and thing

bools.name: dgdAnuVoiceOfLeaders
bools.comment: his voice is the voice of all leaders; beings save vs magic at -4 to resist his commands

bools.name: dgdAnuSummonsDragons

bools.name: dgdAnuBrassMace
bools.comment: he uses a brass mace striking for 2-20 plus his bonus of 7

bools.name: dgdAnuCreatedHeavensEarth
bools.comment: Anu is said to have created the heavens and the earth

bools.name: dgdAnuAllBowToAuthority
bools.comment: all the other Babylonian gods bow to his authority

bools.name: dgdAnsharGodOfDarkness

bools.name: dgdAnsharDarkSkinned

bools.name: dgdDahakAverageIntelligence

col_comments: The roster ordinal cells (the print order, Anu through Ramman)
The print page cells (22-25, the folio offset PRINT = PDF - 1)
The alignment cells (0 lawful good, 1 neutral good, 3 lawful neutral, 4 neutral, 6 lawful evil, 7 neutral evil, 8 chaotic evil)
The rank cells (0 lesser god, 1 greater god, 2 hero, 3 monster format: Gilgamesh the hero, Dahak the monster)
The psionic class cells (6 = the printed class VI of the R849 class table: Anu and Anshar; 0 = Nil)
The plane cells (1 Nirvana, 2 Pandemonium, 3 Nine Hells, 4 Seven Heavens, 5 Elysium, 6 Arcadia, 7 Hades, 8 Concordant Opposition; 0 = none printed: the Dahak monster row and the Gilgamesh hero row)

The fixed-damage cells (1 = a printed damage figure instead of by weapon type: Anu 2-20+7, Dahak 3-30 x3, Druaga 35, Gilgamesh 2-20+8, Girru 1-8+12 / 2-20+12, Ramman 30; the four See below / Nil rows read 0)
The percent-in-lair cells (the Dahak monster-format 25 percent; the deity rows read 0)
The ethereal cells (1 = the Dahak ethereal-except-bite doctrine)
